Shattered Legacy's own music for TazUO, shipped in the player package (cc-P368)
==============================================================================

What is here
------------
  registry.csv   every client music ID we use, one row each (105 to 149; rules at the top of the file).
  tracks\        the mp3 files, tracks\<file>.mp3, one per registry row. GIT-IGNORED: a track is 4 to 25 MB, over the
                 repo's 5 MB rule, so the files live only on the build PC (copied in from D:\UO\third-party\ by
                 Add-Track.ps1) and the registry row carries the SHA-256 the build checks them against.
  Add-Track.ps1  copies a chosen track in, renamed sl-<pack>-<name>.mp3, and writes its registry row with the hash.
                 Run it only for a track Chase marked Use in the Music Room (web console /music, docs\music\
                 music-notes.json in the docs repo), and only after checking its terms below.

How it reaches the player (nothing of EA's is shipped or changed):
  Build-PlayerPackage.ps1 stages app\music\<file>.mp3 for every row (gate 3 checks each byte for byte, gate 4 checks the
  zip holds exactly the registry's files and their hashes) and writes app\music\shard-music.txt, one Config.txt line
  per track: "<id> <file>.mp3,loop". At every start, Play.ps1's Build-UoOverrides.ps1 appends those lines to a copy of
  the player's own Music\Digital\Config.txt (app\uo-overrides\Music\Digital\Config.txt; a stock line is never changed,
  and an ID the player's file already uses is skipped with a yellow line) and hands TazUO an override for the copy
  ("music/digital/config.txt=...") and one per track ("music/digital/<file>.mp3=<app\music\file.mp3>"). TazUO asks its
  file override map for both paths (Sound.GetMusic -> FileManager.GetUOFilePath("Music/Digital/<name>.mp3"), and
  SoundsLoader.Load for "Music/Digital/Config.txt", at client pin 3212623f), so the mp3 plays from app\music\ and the
  player's Music folder is never written. The server plays an ID with the ordinary play-music packet (0x6D).

Credits and terms
-----------------
Every track we may ship comes from one of these four community packs (D:\UO\third-party\<folder>\SOURCE.txt has the
download record for each). None states a license. They are treated as community work: credit the author, ship only
inside the player package or the private repo, never repost. The stock Ultima Online music they remix or replace is
EA's, so the package is the only place they go.

  Zigholtul      UO Classic Music (SOS Mix) Vol.2 (servuo.dev resource 2682, posted 2026-09-30): 93 tracks,
                 D:\UO\third-party\sos-music-vol2\. "Another plug-in-play audio swap of the default UO stock music."
                 UO Classic Music (SOS Mix) + DLC 1.2 (servuo.dev resource 2665, updated 2026-09-11): 117 tracks,
                 D:\UO\third-party\sos-music-dlc\. The author's own picks under the stock file names.
                 Zigholtul is also the author of the paperdoll art we ship (vendor\paperdoll-sos\SOURCE.txt).
  ParanoiaPhD    Some uo music remixes 1 (servuo.dev resource 2063, posted 2023-11-27; "IceYouMusic"): 49 remixes of
  (IceYouMusic)  the stock UO MIDI tracks, D:\UO\third-party\paranoia-remixes\. EA-derived audio.
                 Custom Turfin replacement 1 (servuo.dev resource 2142, posted 2024-03-10): 1 track,
                 D:\UO\third-party\paranoia-turfin\.

Both authors are credited in the package's README.txt ("What is in here") whenever a track of theirs ships, and each
registry row names its author and pack.

FLAGGED: possibly from another game. Check before shipping.
----------------------------------------------------------
The SOS DLC's SOURCE.txt flags the pack as likely holding music from other games ("personalized selections"), and the
Music Room (cc-P367) read every file's ID3 album tag: 197 of the 353 tracks on disk carry an album that does not name
Ultima ("not tagged Ultima" on the page). The most common: Oblivion (16), Youtube (12), Diablo 2 (10), Fallout 1 (8),
Ni No Kuni (7), Dark Souls 1 (7), South Park: The Stick of Truth (7). Two examples: SOS DLC's Turfin.mp3 is tagged
"Optimistic" from Digimon, and AnvilStrikeInMinoc.mp3 is "The Strongholds" from Kingdoms of Amalur. The badge is not a
verdict (some albums are "Youtube", "Wanderer" or "Origin Audio CD Vol. 2"), so the rule is:

  A track whose album tag, or whose SOURCE.txt, points at another game or composer is NOT shipped until Chase has
  checked it and said so in the Music Room note for that track. Add-Track.ps1 refuses a source whose album tag lacks
  "Ultima" unless -Checked is given, and records the album in the registry row's source column either way.

The Paranoia remixes and Turfin are remixes of EA's own compositions (SOURCE.txt), not other games' music; the
"not tagged Ultima" badge on those reflects their tags, not their source.

Shipped tracks
--------------
None yet (2026-10-21): no track is marked Use in the Music Room. When one is, this section gets a block per track:
the registry row, the original file and its tag, who cleared it and when, and where the server plays it.
